# Only admins can merge (decrypt + re-sign the rebased entries). When the merging
# identity is a non-admin, the audit-log driver aborts and the merge fails.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# bob is a dev (non-admin) but a recipient of the audit key, so he can decrypt
# the log - he just may not merge it.
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add bob'

# Two log-only divergences so the audit-log driver is invoked on merge.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group-add ops
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: bob += ops'

exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group-add sec
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: bob += sec'

# Merge as bob (non-admin): the driver decrypts the log but refuses to merge.
exec git checkout ours
env SESAM_ID=$BOB_KEY
! exec git merge theirs
stderr 'not an admin'
